Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General

Topic 12.2: Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poems, Songs and Tongue Twisters
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poems, Songs and Tongue Twisters, part of ENVIRONMENTAL POLLUTION Suggested Vocabulary: environment, atmosphere, conserve, in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: What can you learn from poems and songs? 2. Which poems and songs do you know? 3. How do you tell the meaning of unfamiliar words while reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poems, Songs and Tongue Twisters together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Responsibility is promoted when learners read poems/listen to songs and answer questions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Environmental Education is enhanced as the learner interacts with content on environmental pollution.

• Life Skills Education – Communication skills are enhanced as the learner recites poems and sing songs.

Link to other Subjects:

The learner relates the content of songs and poems to what is learnt in Music.

The learner applies the content of Environmental Pollution to a concept learnt in in Integrated Science.
